findings.text: §9 states that "§7 has six to repair beyond its own three" out of the seven names it hands over, but two of those seven, `coolant_absorbed_energy_accumulated_of_plasma_facing_component` and `volume_averaged_electron_number_density_over_scrape_off_layer`, are the names the lead's 2026-11-12 ruling holds from the next cut (comment `c-s7-lead-ruling-sourceless`, plan.html:126), and §7's done-when excludes "the names held from the release under the lead's rulings" from its repair population; §7 therefore repairs four and lists two as held, not six

findings.reason: the plant is the only control for the exemption, and as worded it is satisfiable only by planting a case that is not the one the rule covers or by implementing a broader exemption than §7's.
findings.text: the seventh plant is "a live name of derived origin with no producer edge" that must be "listed apart as an exempt derived parent", but the exemption §7 states is for derived parents, not for names of derived origin: a planted name carrying origin `derived` with no live child is not a derived parent, so a count built to §7's rule counts it and reports 3, or the node widens the exemption to every derived-origin name and its guard no longer matches the rule it is testing

findings.reason: the node must write one assertion for the live-graph number and the plan permits either 9 or 10, so the gate it writes can pass a reading the plan did not mean.
findings.text: the live-graph clause requires the command to report "the same number and the same names as a direct read of producer edges … (10 on 2026-11-14)" while the same sentence requires `beta`, one of those ten, to be listed apart from the count, and the plant fixes the reporting convention so that a counted set of two with one listed apart reports 2; on the live graph the command therefore reports 9 against a direct edge read of 10, so the agreement clause as worded cannot be asserted alongside the exemption clause
